scope: finite model NotificationHandoff: one tenant and two events of one source. Case one-recipient: one recipient, both events strong and sharing one replace key, a minimum interval of two ticks over three instants, at most two beats and two delivery tries for each unit. Case no-replace-key: one recipient, no replace key, one strong event, one delivery try, two beats; two notifications can be live together, so a beat can carry more than one. Case two-recipients: two recipients, one strong event, one delivery try, no beat; it checks that boxes, units and pacing of two recipients do not interfere. Each action is one commit of its owner. The session intake is modelled only as a set that recalls by submission id; subscriptions, qualification, several destinations for one recipient, retry back-off and standing items are not modelled. Safety only: nothing here shows that a strong notification is eventually delivered. No refinement proof to the implementation.

mutations.name: supersede-only-unresolved
mutations.old: Supersedes(e2, r) == e2 \in Keyed /\ Has(e2, r)
mutations.new: Supersedes(e2, r) == e2 \in Keyed /\ Has(e2, r) /\ resolved[e2][r] = "none"

mutations.name: unit-membership-not-recorded
mutations.old: InSomeUnit(e, r) == \E u \in units : u.kind = "strong" /\ u.r = r /\ e \in u.members
